content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text labels the Romans 1:3 issue UNDERDETERMINED because there is no explicit textual resolution of paternity, which is the kind of non-statement ground the rule governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D6 vs C4 (Romans 1:3): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open.","room":"without explicit textual resolution of paternity: one reading is that lack of an explicit statement in the relevant verse cannot support UNDERDETERMINED under K-S2; the other is that weighing multiple verses with no explicit resolution may support UNDERDETERMINED. The judge text uses the second reading.","why":"It uses the absence of an explicit textual resolution of paternity as the reason for UNDERDETERMINED, contrary to K-S2's bar on treating a verse's non-statement as such a ground."}
